Vyzhnytsia Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Vyzhnytsia — known to Hasidim worldwide as Vizhnitz — was the birthplace of the Vizhnitz Hasidic dynasty, founded here in 1854 by Rabbi Menachem-Mendel Hager and today one of the largest Hasidic movements globally, with major communities still active in Israel and the United States. The town's Jewish population surged after the dynasty's founding, reaching a peak of 5,080 people — 89 percent of the population — by 1910, alongside the separately prominent Sadigur and Boyan Hasidic dynasties and eight profession-specific synagogues. By August 1941, some 1,820 Jews had been deported to Transnistria, with the remainder following that October; only 800 remained by 1945, and by 1990 just three Jewish families were left in what had once been a major center of Hasidic Judaism. This cemetery, marked on an 1860s Austrian map and presumably operating until the late 19th century, was likely demolished after WWII and built over during the Soviet era; a school and its sports yard now occupy the site.
